newsitem.title: USA: Pact for new NYC's new finance agency seen closer.
newsitem.headline: Pact for new NYC's new finance agency seen closer.

text.p: New York City and New York State had not solved all their conflicts over a new borrowing arm for the city on late Friday but a agreement still was expected as soon as next week, sources close to the talks said.

"The discussions broke off after another meeting today with no final agreement, but I think the pieces are coming together," said a city source, who declined to be named. And he cautioned that the deal still might fall apart, a not uncommon occurrence in Albany.
Among the main obstacles that remain outstanding are a split over what to exent the local finance laws that cover municipalities should apply to the new infrastructure authority.
The new borrowing authority would sell up to $7.5 billion of bonds over the next four years to pay for maintaining and improving New York City's overcrowded schools and stressed infrastructure.

New York State would have to approve the creation of such a new authority, which the Giuliania Administration wants so that it can sidestep a state-imposed debt cap. The city is expected to reach its debt ceiling about one month before the end of its fiscal year on June 30.

Local finance laws, which impose limits on the debt issued by municipalities, have prompted conflicts over which rules should apply to the new authority, which will repay its debt using revenues from the city's personal income taxes.
These debt regulations cover a range of issues, such as the economic life of what is financed, debt limits and whether variable-rate debt can be sold.
"The city was willing to have (some rules) apply to the finance authority, but there were cases where it wouldn't make sense," the city source said.
